No marketing spin.What is MISFITZ?+MISFITZ is a true extraction game, the first one built natively for mobile. Free to play on iOS and Android. High-stakes 5-to-10 minute runs where 16 players drop into a live world, loot Relics, and decide whether to team up with strangers or betray them at the extraction point. Die before you extract and you lose everything. No energy systems.How is MISFITZ different from Arena Breakout or Tarkov?+Arena Breakout and Tarkov are hardcore military simulations. 30 to 45 minute sessions, FPS controls, deep inventory systems, the works. MISFITZ is built around a different question: what does extraction look like when the screen is small, the session is short, and your friends are around. Top-down perspective. Auto-aim. 5 to 10 minute runs. The skill ceiling is positioning and reading other players, not flick-aim. It is not a casual game though. The pre-alpha hit an 80.5% retry rate after death — short sessions concentrate the tension, they don't dilute it.How does the alliance and betrayal system work?+Anyone can propose an alliance with anyone, mid-run. If both players accept, you team up. Either side can break the alliance at any time, but it doesn't end instantly. IOS & ANDROID.What is MISFITZ?MISFITZ is a true extraction game, the first one designed natively for mobile. It implements every defining feature of the extraction genre: drop-in raids, real loss on death, persistent loadouts, PvPvE tension, and extraction points in a persistent world. It is not extraction-like or extraction-adjacent. It is also the most social take on the genre: 16-player matches where alliances, cooperation, and betrayal between strangers are core mechanics, not side features. MISFITZ is built by Antihero Studios in Barcelona, a team of former Supercell developers (Brawl Stars, Clash Royale) and former King developers (Candy Crush), backed by $4.5M in seed funding. MISFITZ is free on iOS and Android. Runs are 5 to 10 minutes. Players loot Relics, form alliances, and choose to cooperate or betray before extracting. But around us, too much of the industry was drifting somewhere else: fake ads, shitty games, and players losing a little more trust in mobile gaming every year.
